finding.claim: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is not enforced cumulatively for chunked requests (no Content-Length). Streaming path (__anext__) and buffered path (__await__) never cap total bytes, so an unauthenticated client can push unbounded body data into memory (urlencoded/get_data) or disk (multipart file parts) for up to BODY_TIMEOUT (60s) per request.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP client sending POST with Transfer-Encoding: chunked to any route that reads request.form, request.files, get_data() or json (src/quart/asgi.py:63-67 queues every chunk into Body with no size accounting).
finding.sink: Body queue memory (src/quart/wrappers/request.py:110-111) and multipart stream_factory disk writes (src/quart/formparser.py:165-179, 208).

trace.note: http.request chunks put into request.body without size accounting
Only check is declared Content-Length > max; chunked requests have none, so _must_raise is never set
__anext__ streaming path has no cumulative size check
Multipart parser iterates body via async for, i.e. the streaming path
File parts written via stream_factory with no size cap
__await__ buffered path checks max only after full body is already queued in memory
BODY_TIMEOUT (60s, app.py:226) wraps _load_form_data; bounds time, not size

finding.guards_checked: MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH (16MB, app.py:230) compared only against declared Content-Length (request.py:65-70) and post-buffer (request.py:102-106); BODY_TIMEOUT 60s (app.py:226, request.py:359) bounds duration only; MAX_FORM_MEMORY_SIZE (500000) applies to non-file field data only (formparser.py:211-214); MAX_FORM_PARTS limits part count only. Not verified: get_data() path under BODY_TIMEOUT; werkzeug MultipartDecoder second argument semantics (formparser.py:188 passes max_content_length, which may be max_form_memory_size; werkzeug not in repo).
